VASSAL.build.module.folder.ModuleSubFold.desc: Change entries by version; GitHub issues: github.com/RiverWanderer-Vassal/ccnapoleonicsEpic/issues
VASSAL.build.module.folder.ModuleSubFold.name: Change Log
a01 #7 EPIC17 Dresden (Day 1) setup: removed extra French Victory Banner from French VB slot 14
a02 Change log added as buildFile folders
a03 Change log entries cross-referenced to GitHub issues
a04 #1 Battalion Mass set up when French move first: Battalion Mass Setup added to Game Start-French
a05 #4 Attack marker cleared (attack cancelled, logged) if the declared attacker moves before combat dice are rolled
a06 #4 No log line for the implicit attack cancel (same as replacing an unused Attack marker)
a07 #5 cName (and name) initialised at every launch via chkSTART; setRole still sets them on side change
a08 #5 Launch init builds cName privately (chkSTART on cName setprop only); shared Global Controls name no longer written at load
a09 #3 End-turn square card return: targets the square track map, matches SqMarker for the side that just ended its turn
a10 #9 Square track slots 7-8 reinstated as spares: zone SqMarker AlliesSq7/8, FrenchSq7/8; FrenchSq8 icon fixed
a11 #10 Hasty Square: card picks the highest free slot (8 down) and passes it to the unit; take-back unsquares the unit; square marker layer extended to 8
a11 #3 Square slot search skips a slot whose card is still on the track (no same-turn reuse before end-turn return)
a12 #10 Hasty Square card clears its slot when discarded (a redrawn card could otherwise unsquare a unit)
a12 #3 a11 card-on-slot check removed (not needed); slot search is first free flag 1-8
a12 #11 Square limits: max squares = Command - 1 enforced (Hasty Square excepted); alert texts corrected (1 card must stay in hand)
a13 #11 Max squares is a Grand Battles rule: limit = Command (not Command - 1), checked only when isGB; no max-squares check in Epic; alert: Squares at maximum (Hasty Square excepted)
a14 #11 Alert wording: Squares are at maximum (Hasty Square excepted); Hand is at minimum size - square not allowed (Hasty Square excepted)
a15 #11 Min-hand alert text re-set at every launch (Startup, SetPrefs): GP values are saved in setups, so the a12 default change did not reach refreshed games
a16 #10 Hasty Square take-back fixed: drag into a hand triggers on moveInHand (hands do not send mapMove); side recorded at play (hsSide) and used to find the unit
a17 #11 Square alert texts re-set by Refresh (VassalPostRefreshGHK on cSqLimitAlrt, gAlliesSqAlertMsg, gFrenchSqAlertMsg); a15 Startup re-set removed (piece traits in unrefreshed saves are stale)

a17 #5 Role flags (isObserver, isCorpsCmdr, isCiC, isSolitaire, isNotSolitaire) also set on chkSTART at every launch - Flip Cards was enabled for Solitaire after reload; Allies Commander Flip report guarded for blank handOpen
a18 #10 Hasty Square take-back drag trigger: stray escape removed from GetMapProperty comma (Bad Data on moveInHand)
a19 #11 Min-hand alert reads [hand] is at minimum size...; hand report names: Allies Hand or French Hand, Corps hands Allies Hand (Left) etc. - re-set on Refresh (Global Controls fixHandNames)
a20 #10 Card back in hand handled by the move key (moveInHand): Take to Hand only moves the card; TC marker removed from Main Map and Hasty Square unit unsquared on drag or Take to Hand
a21 #10 Hasty Square play actions run once: moving the played card on the board no longer re-finds a slot (which broke the drag-back unsquare)
a22 #13 Add Russian banner to EPIC15 Friedland (only)
a23 #10 Hasty Square take-back rebuilt on the move key: slot cleared whenever the card enters a hand or is discarded (no stale slot), unit unsquared only if the card came from the battlefield
a24 #10 Hasty Square take-back rebuilt on the move key: slot cleared whenever the card enters a hand or is discarded (no stale slot), unit unsquared only if the card came from the battlefield

VASSAL.build.module.folder.ModuleSubFold.name: a01 #17 Napoleon's initial discard uses the normal discard and report
a02 #13 Starting banners corrected: EPIC12 Laon +2 Prussian; GB04 Talavera +1 British (stray unconverted banner removed); GB07 Salamanca duplicate banner removed

a02 #12 Re-snap to hex centres (army and terrain): 26 setups corrected by position edit only (no move commands, so no terrain replacement); EPIC13-22, Dresden, GB/MD and other on-grid setups unchanged
a02 EPIC13 Eylau menu entry pointed back to EpicEylau.vsav (was set to CCNapoEpic4alpha.vmod, not in the module) #29
a03 Terrain charts: third tab Field Works Diagrams (2-, 3- and 4-sided Field Works facing examples)

a05 #8 Special Rules charts redrawn from the Grand Battles rules (GMT 2025): Victory Banner Objectives, EPIC, Grand Battles 1st and 2nd Edition, National Rules and Iconic Commanders, Garrisons, Grand Battery and Leaders
a06 #8 National Rules chart: Mother Russia Infantry and Flag results no longer state that the added block adds a combat die
a07 #8 National Rules chart: Mother Russia results apply only as allowed in the scenario Special Rules, otherwise ignored
a08 #8 National Rules chart: Archduke John portrait added next to Archduke Charles in Iconic Commanders
a09 #8 National Rules chart: Archduke John given his own Iconic Commanders row, portrait sized and placed as the others
a10 #8 National Rules chart: Charles and John back on one row, portraits side by side, left-aligned with the other leaders
a11 #8 National Rules chart: Charles and John entry now says add Hungarian marker, +1 in ranged and melee combat
a14 #14 Take to Hand of a played Command card restores the hand (played flag, CiC play status, square buttons): a stale card handCase no longer blocks the move-in-hand actions
a14 #16 Tactician mark on a unit kept when a declared attack is cancelled because the attacker moves (e.g. Light Infantry Skirmish move back)
a15 #16 Attack marker dropped back on its own hex is ignored (no re-opened attack or Bonus Combat); Bonus Combat only when the marker is moved from another hex onto the attacker
a16 #16 Moving the Attack marker to another unit before the dice resets the previous attacker but keeps its Tactician mark (combat marker handling never clears Tactician marks)
a17 #19 Help > Report an Issue opens the GitHub bug form with module, VASSAL, Java and OS versions, scenario and game state filled in; alpha/beta go to labels (were added to assignees)
a18 #22 Terrain charts: Hill Line of Sight Diagrams tab added between Page 2 and Field Works Diagrams (Plateau and Same Hill, Artillery Firing Over); Field Works Diagrams unchanged

a19 #23 Leader names converted on Refresh (as standard v4.2.10 Convert Leaders): Refresh sends initMarker then shortName to every Class LDR piece, so LeaderName is set from the label or BasicName and dName follows; fixes unnamed leaders in reports and the doubled Leader of Honor set-up label (MM13 Blake)

4.0.6 release: 2026 Army Reference Cards, Combat Tables and Terrain Tile Effects Chart (a03, a04, a12, a13) deferred to 4.0.7; those charts are the 2023 versions with corrections: Terrain - Sand Quarry Inf 0/-1 (note 3) into, 0 out, Arty -1 into; Marsh impassable for artillery (Must Stop note 8, Out Arty NA); notes 3, 7 and 8 updated. Russian Light Infantry (and Suvorov) movement 1 / 2 NB; Russian Heavy Cuirassier is CU; British Rocket Artillery movement 1-2 NB. Leader portraits Blücher, Bülow, Röder, Württemberg and Dupont de l’Étang stored under the names the module uses, so they display

VASSAL.build.module.map.CounterDetailVie.summaryReportFormat:
{tStyleINF + BasicName + tBlockFmt + tBlock.repeat(Strength) + tNoBlockFont + tBlock.repeat(MaxStrength-Strength) + tHdgINF + (BasicName =~ ".*Light.*|.*Young.*" ? "1
2" + pNoBattle : "1") + GetProperty("pUflag"+IgnoreFLG) + (Retreat1 != "" ? Retreat1 + "→" + Retreat : Retreat) + "" + rngMax + "" + (rngStBonus > 0 ? Strength + "+" + (rngStBonus) + "" : (Strength + rngBonus)) + "" + (Type == "Unit" ? (Math.max(0,(Strength + rngRnd)/2 + rngBonus- rngMvMalus)) : "NA") + "" + (BasicName == "Prussian Line Infantry" || BasicName == "French Line Infantry" ? Strength + "+1" : (Strength+ccBonus)) + (ccMvMalus != 0 ? "" + (-ccMvMalus) + "" : "") + "" + (NoXSW ? "No Saber hits except on Leaders." : "") + GetProperty("tNote" + BasicName)}

{tStyleCAV + BasicName + tBlockFmt + tBlock.repeat(Strength) + tNoBlockFont + tBlock.repeat(MaxStrength-Strength) + tHdgCAV +(BasicName.contains("Light") ? "1-3" : "1-2") + GetProperty("pUflag"+IgnoreFLG) + (Retreat1 != "" ? Retreat1 + ";" + Retreat : Retreat) + "" + (Strength + ccBonus) + "" + (NoXSW || LNCR_Level == 1 || CU_Level == 1 || COS_Level == 1 ? "" : "") + (NoXSW ? "No Saber hits except on Leaders" : CU_Level == 1 ? "Ignore 1 hit from Ranged Infantry
Lancers do not reroll flags" : "") + (MLNCR_Level == 1 || COS_Level == 1 ? "
" : "") + (LNCR_Level == 1 || MLNCR_Level == 1 ? "Reroll flags when attacking or
First Strike, except vs Curaissiers" : COS_Level == 1 ? "Ignore Forest dice reduction
Does not count as a Victory Banner" : "")}

{tStyleART + BasicName + tBlockFmt + tBlock.repeat(Strength) + tNoBlockFont + tBlock.repeat(MaxStrength-Strength) + tHdgART + (BasicName =~ ".*Horse.*" ? (Strength==1 ? "1-2" + pNoBattle : "1
2" + pNoBattle) : RB_Level == 1 ? "1-2"+ pNoBattle : "1" + pNoBattle) + GetProperty("pUflag"+IgnoreFLG) + (Retreat1 != "" ? Retreat1 + ";" + Retreat : Retreat) + "" + (GetProperty("rngART"+(Strength==1?2:1)) + ccBonus) + "     " + GetProperty("rngART"+(Strength==1?3:2)) + "" + GetProperty("rngART"+(Strength==1?4:3)) + "" + (rngMax==4 && Strength > 1 ? pStop + "
1" : GetProperty("rngART"+(Strength==1?5:4))) + "" + GetProperty("rngART"+(Strength==1?6:5)) +"" + (RB_Level == 1 ? "Special rules apply: see Allies-British Chart [F1]" : "")}

VASSAL.build.module.StartupGlobalKeyComm.name: Start up message & set global constants (Vassal workaround to allow maintenance of GPs used as constants in pre-set scenarios)
VASSAL.build.module.StartupGlobalKeyComm.reportFormat:
{!prefNoWelcome ?Alert("

Commands & Colors: Napoleonics Epic & Grand Battles, Version 4

This module release automates card handling and enhances marker functionality for ease of play. It is similar in use to Version 4 of the standard module.

The Allies or French player may set the game to allow a different player count from the default (Epic only); each Corps Commander player must also press the Join Game button on screen or in that Corps Commander's hand window.

6/8 Player games only: Commander-in-Chief (Allies and French) allocates Tactician Card draws when prompted, by button press or equivalent right-click command.

To start a game, the \"Move First\" C-i-C player presses the \"Deal Cards\" button or equivalent right-click command.

Hints & Tips
Card Play: Use the right-click commands to play Cards. This avoids potential for cards to be placed into the wrong part of the board which can compromise automated card management for End Turn and Counter-attack functions.

Stacking: Most commands are available from the topmost stacked piece but to access a stacked unit, select the stack and press left-arrow. To re-stack, press left-arrow again. Some commands automatically re-stack.

General: Unit and Leader commands are context sensitive by default. This keeps menus short and reduces errors. This means that some commands are only available before a unit is Ordered (March Move, Garrison - where valid - and Recover Hit) or when a unit has a combat marker on it (e.g. Take Hits and Square). Press F1 for a list of common commands and shortcuts.

This welcome message can be disabled from Preferences, Game Options.... Find further assistance via the resources under the Help drop-down menu.

"):""}

VASSAL.build.module.RandomTextButton.faces: Multiple hits can be applied in one command via the Attacker and Target markers.,In an opposed game\, players can apply hits and other combat commands without selecting the piece. See the Shortcuts help sheet [F1].,All card draws are automatic. Players may draw additional cards manually (see Scenario Notes if this applies). [Shift+F1],A Tactician Card may be drawn manually\, if a player forgets to set the option from a "Command Stars" card.,Special game counters may be drawn from the Markers palette [hotkey: F4] to form a stock on the player's side of the board. Counter stocks each have a right-click menu to draw or add counters.,Use the right-click menus to play cards. These ensure that cards are played to the correct locations. To make a correction\, drag the card from one section to the other.,Mother Russia: Drag a "Paper-Strength" counter onto a Russian FA\, LN or LT unit to upgrade that unit. Right-click to convert the counter to a Cossack or Fieldworks piece instead.,Press F1 to pull up the charts window. One of the charts lists the module's hotkeys and command shortcuts.,To show or hide your hand window\, press the Escape key or\, during a game\, click on your player seat icon.,Simply press the Squaring button in your hand window to put your targeted infantry unit into square. For Battalion Mass\, click on your side's count of Battalion Mass markers.,Player Command Size and Tactician hand size are displayed on the Wellington and Napoleon player seat icons around the board.,Hidden command Ctrl+Shift+H will eliminate the unit.,Left-click on a counter store to draw or play a counter as applicable. [Preferences...Game Options: Mouse-Click Counter Actions],Hidden hotkeys Alt+Q and Alt+T will generate another quote and module tip respectively. Quotes are largely apocryphal!,Several features can be tailored to your needs via Preferences...Game Options tab.,Sound is optional and can be turned on or off for this module on the Preferences...Sounds tab.,Combat markers can be placed by drag and drop as well as by using the right-click menu or left-click on a piece.,The active Commander-in-Chief ends the turn from their hand window or hotkey [F12]. If you might forget an end turn action\, there is also the option to set a reminder.,The Help toolbar menu lists several useful resources for playing the game and using this module.,Zoom the current map in or out using Hotkeys Ctrl+[ and Ctrl+]. To quickly adjust a map window to your monitor\, try the "fit" options under the magnifying glass toolbar button.,Commanders-in-Chief can claim a Victory Banner by left-clicking on the banner icon next to their Army name. Click on a deployed Victory Banner to remove it.,Game clocks when enabled will keep approximate track of each side's playing time during an online game. F8 will pause clocks. Clicking on a clock will switch the timer over (normally automatic).,To detach a leader without marking the unit\, right-click on the leader piece and select the special command "Detach Leader" (shortcut: Alt+D).,Use left-arrow to access a unit and its right-click menu beneath an attached leader.,After playing a card\, left-click on a unit or its attached leader to order that unit. Double-click an ordered unit or attached leader to start combat. [Preferences...Game Options: Mouse-Click Battlefield Actions],Left-click on a unit or leader to place a combat marker (double-click on an attached leader). Attack markers are placed only on ordered units. [Preferences...Game Options: Mouse-Click Battlefield Actions],Clearing an Attack marker will reset Mouse-Click to "ordering mode". [Preferences...Game Options: Mouse-Click Battlefield Actions] ,The introductory tutorial demonstrates key features. See Help... from the main toolbar.,See Help...Release Notes for detailed information about the module.,For best effect\, apply hits\, Leader Check and retreats in sequence per rules and use the combat marker "Take Hits" menu or equivalent key commands.,Avoid trying to move or select the same piece as another player. Let the active Commander-in-Chief coordinate the turn as necessary.,Combat actions can be performed via hotkeys (no piece selected). See Shortcuts [F1].
VASSAL.build.module.RandomTextButton.name: Module Tips

VASSAL.build.module.RandomTextButton.faces: Sometimes a single battle decides everything and sometimes\, too\, the slightest circumstance decides the issue of a battle.,Doctors will have more lives to answer for in the next world than even we generals.,I love a brave soldier who has undergone the baptism of fire.,If you had seen one day of war\, you would pray to God that you would never see another.,In war\, as in politics\, no evil - even if it is permissible under the rules - is excusable unless it is absolutely necessary. Everything beyond that is a crime.,In war\, morale factors acount for three quarters of the whole; relative material strength accounts for only one quarter.,Remember \, gentlemen\, what a Roman emperor said: The corpse of an enemy always smells sweet.,There is a moment in every battle at which the least manoeuvre is decisive and gives superiority\, as one drop of water causes overflow.,An army marches on its stomach.,An army's effectiveness depends on its size\, training\, experience\, and morale\, and morale is worth more than any of the other factors combined.,Between a battle lost and a battle won\, the distance is immense and there stand empires.,Courage is like love: it must have hope for nourishment.,Every soldier carries a marshal's baton in his pack.,God is on the side with the best artillery.,He that makes war without many mistakes has not made war very long.,How many things apparently impossible have nevertheless been performed by resolute men who had no alternative but death.,I have made all the calculations\, fate will do the rest.,If the art of war were nothing but the art of avoiding risks\, glory would become the prey of mediocre minds.,If they want peace\, nations should avoid the pin-pricks that precede cannonshots.,If you wage war\, do it energetically and with severity. This is the only way to make it shorter and consequently less inhuman.,In time of revolution\, with perseverance and courage\, a soldier should think nothing impossible.,In war there is but one favorable moment; the great art is to seize it!,In war\, three-quarters turns on personal character and relations; the balance of manpower and materials counts only for the remaining quarter.,It should not be believed that a march of three or four days in the wrong direction can be corrected by a countermarch. As a rule\, this is to make two mistakes instead of one.,One bad general is worth two good ones.,Read over and over the campaigns of Alexander\, Hannibal\, Caesar\, Gustavus\, Turenne\, Eugene and Frederic. This is the only way to become a great general and master the secrets of the art of war.,Soldiers generally win battles; generals get credit for them.,Strategy is the art of making use of time and space. I am less concerned about the later than the former. Space we can recover\, lost time never.,The basic principle that we must follow in directing the armies of the Republic is this: that they must feed themselves on war at the expense of the enemy territory.,The morale is to the physical as three to one.,The most important qualification of a soldier is fortitude under fatigue and privation. Courage is only second; hardship\, poverty and want are the best school for a soldier.,The secret of war lies in the communications.,There are certain things in war of which the commander alone comprehends the importance. Nothing but his superior firmness and ability can subdue and surmount all difficulties.,There are in Europe many good generals\, but they see too many things at once. I see one thing\, namely the enemy's main body. I try to crush it\, confident that secondary matters will then settle themselves.,There are only two forces in the world\, the sword and the spirit. In the long run the sword will always be conquered by the spirit.,Once I have made up my mind\, everything is forgotten except what leads to success.,There is no man more pusillanimous than I when I am planning a campaign. I purposely exaggerate all the dangers and all the calamities that the circumstances make possible.,To have good soldiers\, a nation must always be at war.,Two armies are two bodies which meet and try to frighten each other.,Victory belongs to the most persevering.,What my enemies call a general peace is my destruction. What I call peace is merely the disarmament of my enemies. Am I not more moderate than they?,You do not get peace by shouting: Peace. Peace is a meaningless word; what we need is a glorious peace.,You must not fight too often with one enemy\, or you will teach him all your art of war.,A general-in-chief should ask\, What should I do if the enemy appeared now in my front\, or on my right\, or on my left?,A rapid march increases all the chances of victory.,When an army is inferior in number\, in cavalry and in artillery\, it is essential to avoid a general action.,If you want to avoid a battle with a superior army\, occupy a good defensive position.,The transition from defensive to offensive is one of the most delicate operations in war.,As far as possible\, the artillery should cover and command the surrounding country.,When you are resolved to fight a battle\, collect your whole force. A single battalion sometimes decides the day.,When you determine to risk a battle\, reserve to yourself every possible chance of success\, more particularly\, if you have to deal with an adversary of superior talent.,Never leave gaps for the enemy to penetrate\, unless it be to draw him into a snare.,Encampments of the same army should be formed so as to protect each other.,Infantry\, cavalry and artillery are nothing without each other.,It is the business of cavalry to follow up the victory\, and to prevent the beaten army from rallying.,Artillery is more essential to cavalry than to infantry\, because cavalry has no fire for its defence.,Artillery should always be placed in the most advantageous positions\, and as far in front of the line of cavalry and infantry\, without comprising the safety of the guns\, as possible.,It depends on the general alone to conquer difficulties by superior talent and resolution.,The science of strategy is only to be acquired by experience\, and by studying the campaigns of all the great captains.,Once the offensive has been assumed\, it must be sustained to the last.,To advance or not to advance is a matter for grave consideration.,Even in offensive warfare in the open field the great secret consists in defensive combats\, and in obliging the enemy to attack.,It is an approved maxim in war\, never to do what the enemy wishes you to do.,Nothing is so important in war as an undivided command.,Never interrupt your enemy when he is making a mistake.,The battlefield is a scene of constant chaos. The winner will be the one who controls that chaos\, both his own and the enemy’s.,Give me lucky generals.
